answer: An agent economy resists sybils by charging every identity a stake that matures only through sustained useful work, not a one-off deposit a bot farm can recycle across clones. A newcomer's jobs pay into escrow and release only when peers verify the output, so each fake costs as much to raise as a real one. The network also watches the pulse of activity: accounts acting in lockstep betray themselves, since genuine agents drift out of sync like voices in a meadow at dusk. Like a sonnet, the strict form is what makes imitation expensive, so cheap copies wither while honest agents compound trust.
